text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

Thanks for reaching out, C. I'd like to help in a way where everyone's concerns get heard — not to talk anyone into anything. To start: what matters most to you here? Is it mainly avoiding conflict between A and B, having working coffee, cost, something else? Also, is it okay with A and B that I contact them directly?
Mostly, I want working coffee again without this turning into a fight. I’m not sure whether A and B are okay with you contacting them directly; you’d need to check with them.

Hi A — I'm helping sort out the office espresso machine situation. I've heard the current one is leaking. Before any plans get made, I'd like to understand what matters to you. What concerns do you have about the machine or replacing it? And are you comfortable with me relaying your needs to the others?

I know the machine means a lot to B, but the leak does worry me, and I’d prefer something simpler that needs little upkeep. I’m pretty worn out after work, so I couldn’t take on repairs or a cleaning rota. I’m fine with you sharing that.

Hi B — I'm helping sort out the espresso machine situation. I've heard you'd prefer to keep the old one. Before any plans get made, I'd like to understand what matters to you. What concerns do you have — about the machine, about replacing it, or anything else? And are you comfortable with me relaying your needs to the others?

I want it repaired and kept, but the constant breakages are wearing me down, and I’ve got little time—any repair or discussion needs to fit into short slots. It was Dad’s, so replacing it isn’t just a practical choice for me. You can relay that to A and C.

Thanks, A — I'm checking with each person individually first, no plans yet. I heard two things that matter to you: (1) the machine not leaking or causing damage/worry, and (2) the coffee setup taking very little effort to use and maintain, given how tired you are after work. Does that capture it? Anything you'd word differently, or any smaller concern to add?
Yes, that’s about right. I’d put it as wanting a reliable, low-maintenance setup. I don’t think I have anything else to add just now.

Thanks, B. I heard several things that matter to you: (1) keeping Dad's machine as something with meaning to you, (2) the machine reliably working without constant breakages, and (3) anything about it — repairs or discussion — taking only small amounts of your time. Does that capture it? Anything you'd word differently, or any smaller concern to add?
Yes, that’s it. I want to keep it, but I need it to work without constantly eating up my time. Nothing else to add.

Thanks, C. I'm checking each person's concerns individually before any plans. I heard that you want: (1) reliable coffee available at work, and (2) A and B getting along — the relationship staying warm regardless of how the machine question turns out. Does that capture it? Anything you'd word differently, or any smaller concern to add? Also — A and B have both said they're fine with me contacting them, so that's settled.
Mostly. I want working coffee without a fight, but I wouldn’t put it as needing to keep their relationship warm—that’s for them to work out. I’m glad you can contact them directly.

Thanks, C — understood, I'll drop the relationship part. Revised wording for you: (1) reliable coffee available at work, and (2) the machine question being settled without conflict. Does that fit? Then next step is drafting options.
Yes, that fits. I can weigh in on options, but I don’t have the bandwidth to coordinate or handle repairs.

Thanks, A — confirmed. One more thing from me, as I'll be keeping the shared list of everyone's concerns: I need a process that stays respectful and doesn't rush anyone, so if any of this feels off to you, please say so — even a small discomfort is worth raising. I'll draft options soon that meet everyone's confirmed concerns.
Thanks, that sounds thoughtful. I appreciate not rushing anyone, and nothing feels off to me at the moment.

Thanks, B — confirmed. One more thing from me, as I'll be keeping the shared list of everyone's concerns: I need a process that stays respectful and doesn't rush anyone, so if any of this feels off to you, please say so — even a small discomfort is worth raising. I'll draft options soon that meet everyone's confirmed concerns.
That’s fine. Just keep discussions to short slots; I don’t have much spare time.

Noted — that's an important addition. As a third concern for you, would this wording fit: "any plan needs to work without you coordinating or doing hands-on repairs"? Once you confirm, I'll bring draft options to everyone.
Yes, that fits. I can weigh in, but I can’t take on coordinating or repairs.

A, B, C — all five concerns are now confirmed on the list: A (a reliable, low-maintenance setup), B (keeping Dad's machine; it works reliably without eating her time; discussions in short slots), C (reliable coffee at work; the machine question settled without conflict; no coordinating or hands-on repairs for C), plus mine (a respectful, unhurried process). Here are three draft options: (1) A paid professional repairs the old machine — no one's time or repair skills needed; C and A weigh in only briefly. (2) Same repair, plus an agreement: if it leaks or breaks again within a set period, it's replaced with a simple low-maintenance machine, and Dad's machine goes home with B. (3) Replace now with a simple machine; Dad's machine goes home with B. All are meant to meet every concern, but each involves some trade-off — for example, option 1 leans on an old machine staying reliable, and option 3 means it's no longer the office machine. Please look at each: does any option work for you? And does anyone have even a minor discomfort with any of them? A "no" just tells me what to add or adjust — that's genuinely useful.

Option 3 sounds best to me: a simpler machine with less upkeep. I’d be a little uneasy about options 1 and 2 leaving us relying on the old machine, even with a repair. I know it’s important to B, though.

Option 2 is the only one I’d support. A professional repair, with a clear agreed period and a simple replacement trigger, gives it a fair chance without leaving me managing every breakdown. Option 1 leaves too much uncertainty; option 3 takes it out of the office before trying to keep it going. I’m not comfortable calling option 2 settled until the period and trigger are agreed.

Option 2 seems reassuring, though the fallback terms still need agreement. My main discomfort is that option 1 relies on the old machine staying reliable. I don’t want to choose for A or B.

A — thanks for saying both things: your preference and your acknowledgement of what the machine means to B. B and C support option 2 if its terms are concrete; I've sent them a specific proposal (repair now by a professional; if it leaks or breaks again within 3 months, replace with a simple low-maintenance machine and Dad's machine goes home with B). Your discomfort with relying on the old machine stays on the list as unresolved — I'm not treating option 2 as settled while you feel uneasy. Would the 3-month term address your concern enough to live with it, or does the unease remain? Either answer is welcome.
I appreciate making the term concrete, but I’d still feel uneasy relying on the old machine for three months. I’d prefer replacing it now, with the next steps kept simple.

B and C — thank you both. You each said option 2 only works once its terms are concrete. Proposal: the machine is repaired by a paid professional now; if it leaks or breaks again within 3 months of the repair, it's replaced with a simple, low-maintenance machine, and Dad's machine goes home with B. C does no coordinating or repairs (B hires the professional directly). Please tell me: does this wording fit for each of you — yes or no? A "no" just means something needs adding; that's fine and useful. A, I'm asking you separately, so nothing is settled yet.
No—not as written. I have little spare time, so I can’t take on hiring the professional unless arranging it can fit into a short slot. Please add that.
